newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds end higher on interbank.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds end higher on interbank.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended higher across the board in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest following a softer interbank rate, dealers said on Thursday.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today after a slight fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.50/98.55 compared with Wednesday's close of S$98.33/98.38, September 2001 at S$97.25/97.30 against S$97.10/97.15 and June 2003 at S$95.25/95.30 from S$95.10/95.15.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 1-7/8 1-3/4 percent versus Wednesday's 2-1/4 2-1/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.78/1.73 percent against Wednesday's yield of 1.89/1.84 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.01/1.96 percent against 2.08/2.03 percent.
